title: Map audio volume to effective DualSense HID ranges
problem: Audio file playback exposes 0–255 even though the DualSense speaker stops responding above 0x64, leaving most of the slider dead and forwarding percentage-like values directly to different HID ranges.
reproduce: On the pinned source, the media player declares a 0–255 slider and the USB and Bluetooth paths forward that number directly. Values 100–255 therefore produce no additional speaker change, matching the reporter's controller observation.
acceptance: The player exposes 0–100 percent, maps 100% to speaker 0x64 and headphone 0x7f, clamps out-of-range input, and uses the conversion in USB and Bluetooth paths for both DualSense models.
repair: Introduce one target-aware percentage converter, use valid maxima in all player and diagnostic controls, and add regression tests for endpoints, midpoint rounding and clamping.

verification.limitations: BCL proves the baseline dead range and all target-specific conversions on the immutable source. The upstream Vitest suite and production web build pass separately. Perceived loudness and macOS endpoint volume still require the reporter's controller.
verification.ownerCheck: Open Audio file playback on the same Mac and controller, confirm the slider reads 0–100, compare 25/50/75/100 for a smooth increase, and report whether 100% now matches the 1 kHz speaker test closely enough. Repeat once over USB and Bluetooth if both are available.

publish.commitMessage: fix(audio): map volume percentage to DualSense ranges
